question: Which Linux companion app track should become the canonical implementation path now that Windows Hub has shipped?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it requires choosing between competing native Linux app architectures and accepting security-sensitive desktop packaging and gateway-control boundaries.

options.title: Promote the C/GTK4 Linux track
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59859 as the canonical Linux app candidate, require focused security/packaging review, and close or explicitly supersede alternatives once the path is confirmed.

options.title: Promote the Rust/GTK4 alternative
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61576 as the canonical Linux app candidate and ask the C/GTK4 track to fold in only the useful reviewed pieces.

options.title: Pause for a short app architecture note
options.body: Keep both PRs unlanded until maintainers write down the Linux companion ownership, packaging, permission, and release criteria.

recommendation.title: Promote the C/GTK4 Linux track
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/59859 as the canonical Linux app candidate, require focused security/packaging review, and close or explicitly supersede alternatives once the path is confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the umbrella issue and gave the clearest product-direction comments about the desired GTK-native Linux app shape.
